subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Apollo Program: Engineering the Moon Shot
description: A quick, practical guide to The Apollo Program: Engineering the Moon Shot.

hook.text: The Saturn V rocket produced 7.5 million pounds of thrust. It remains the most powerful machine ever built.

buildup.text: 400,000 engineers worked on Apollo. The guidance computer had less memory than a modern calculator.

discovery.text: Margaret Hamilton's software saved Apollo 11. Her error-handling code prevented a crash during landing.

twist.text: NASA used slide rules, hand calculations, and physical models. There was no CAD software.

climax.text: Neil Armstrong landed with 25 seconds of fuel remaining. The margin between success and death was razor-thin.

punchline.text: They reached the moon with less tech than your phone.

quiz.question: Whose software saved Apollo 11 from crashing during the moon landing?
